newsitem.title: USA: Florida freeze to cause "some yield loss" - growers.
newsitem.headline: Florida freeze to cause "some yield loss" - growers.

text.p: The unseasonably cold weekend will mean "some loss" of orange juice yield for Florida growers that could force wholesale prices slightly higher, the head of Florida Citrus Mutual said on Monday.

Temperatures early Sunday dipped into the mid-20s throughout much of central Florida, with a small area recording a low of 19 degrees, said Bobby McKown, executive director of the citrus growers' cooperative.

"Our early estimate is that we will have some loss in juice yield, that we'll get less juice from each box of fruit," he said. "It wasn't a killer freeze like in the 1980s. But we'll have some twig and leaf damage, and some damage to speciality fruit that remained on the trees."
McKown said the freezing temperatures covered most of the state's citrus-growing belt, but he could not say how much juice would be lost until growers provide more information.
"It's a big part of the crop, and most of the area was affected," he said.

Early Sunday, temperatures dipped lower than the National Weather Service had forecast, mostly because expected cloud cover failed to move over central Florida. Temperatures remained below the freezing mark for one to eight hours, depending on the location, McKown said.

"We've got a wait-and-see attitude about the damage. Retail prices are already high and we don't see any pressure for retail prices to go up. Wholesale prices could firm up just a little bit as a result of the yield loss."
